cards.hint: Think about the angle between lift and motion.
options: perpendicular to the flight direction
parallel to the flight direction
along the pressure variation path
downward with weight to the ground
cards.quote: Lift is the component of this force perpendicular to the flight direction.
cards.stem: Which way does lift point compared with the flight path?

cards.hint: Recall how lift responds to size changes.
options: directly proportional to the area of the object
inversely related to the size of the object
unaffected by changes in wing surface
equal to pressure times flight speed
cards.quote: Like the other aerodynamic force, drag, the lift is directly proportional to the area of the object.
cards.stem: How does lift change when the reference area grows?

cards.hint: Consider what doubling one factor does.
options: Doubling the area doubles the lift
Doubling the area halves the lift
Doubling the area removes the drag
Halving the area doubles the lift
cards.quote: Doubling the area doubles the lift.
cards.stem: What happens to lift if wing size is made twice as large?

cards.hint: Think about speed and staying aloft near the ground.
options: to keep the lift high
to reduce lift near the ground
to cruise with smaller wings
cards.quote: Takeoff and landing are times of relatively low velocity, so to keep the lift high (to avoid the ground!) designers try to increase the wing area.
cards.stem: Why do designers seek more wing area during takeoff and landing?
